facts.statement: The genus Gongbusaurus was named and described by Dong, Zhou, and Zhang in 1983.
facts.quote: The type species Gongbusaurus shiyii was named and described by Dong, Zhou, and Zhang in 1983.

facts.statement: The genus was originally established based on two small teeth found in the holotype specimen IVPP V9069.
facts.quote: Dong and his coauthors established Gongbusaurus on two small teeth, holotype IVPP V9069

facts.statement: Fossils of the type species were found in the Oxfordian-age Upper Shaximiao Formation in Sichuan, China.
facts.quote: These remains came from the Oxfordian-age Upper Shaximiao Formation in Sichuan, China

facts.statement: A second species, G. wucaiwanensis, was added in 1989 based on a fragmentary skeleton including a partial lower jaw and tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Dong added a second species, "G." wucaiwanensis, in 1989 for a fragmentary skeleton (holotype IVPP 8302)

facts.statement: Gongbusaurus lived between approximately 160 and 157 million years ago during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Gongbusaurus is a genus of ornithischian, perhaps ornithopod, dinosaur that lived between about 160 and 157 million years ago, in the Late Jurassic period.

facts.statement: Based on extrapolation from related species, Gongbusaurus was a small, bipedal herbivore about 1.3 to 1.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Gongbusaurus, by extrapolation from the remains of possible species "G." wucaiwanensis and other basal ornithopods, was a herbivorous bipedal animal around 1.3 to 1.5 m long.

facts.statement: The animal is thought to have been a strong runner.
facts.quote: It would have been a strong runner.

facts.statement: Recent reviews classify Gongbusaurus as a dubious ornithischian and recommend renaming the better-known second species.
facts.quote: The most recent reviews also found the genus to be a dubious ornithischian, and recommended renaming the better-known second species.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Gongbusaurus is an ornithischian or an ankylosaurian, as its teeth resemble those of ankylosaurians like Sarcolestes and Gastonia.
facts.quote: Peter Galton has noted that the teeth on which Gongbusaurus is based resemble those of Sarcolestes and Gastonia, so the genus may actually be an ankylosaurian.

facts.statement: The specific name shiyii is a pun meaning both "junior consultant" and "register of lost objects," referencing how the type teeth were found separately among other collected bones.
facts.quote: As shi yi also can mean "register of lost objects" the specific name is at the same time a pun on the fact that the teeth were later separately found among the assorted bones collected during the dig.

facts.statement: Species based solely on teeth are generally not well accepted in paleontological consensus because dinosaur teeth are not distinctive enough to define a genus.
facts.quote: Las especies basadas en dientes no son bien aceptadas en el consenso paleontológico, debido a lo generalista de la anatomía de los dientes.

facts.statement: It has been proposed to move G. wucaiwanensis to a different genus, with "Eugongbusaurus" suggested as an informal replacement name.
facts.quote: Por eso se ha propuesto que "G." wucaiwanensis sea relegado a otro género. Un posible nombre de reemplazo propuesto es el de "Eugongbusaurus", es usado accidentalmente por el público, pero se lo considera informal.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Gongbusaurus spans from the Bathonian to the Oxfordian stages, between 168.2 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Oxfordian (168.2 to 154.8 million years ago)
